pr_title: Add support for Windows CA certificate store
pr_body:
This PR adds support for the Windows CA certificate store.  It does this by introducing a new store in the default provider which recognises the `capi://` URI scheme. The URI used is just `capi://`, there are no arguments. This new store also becomes the default store when `capistore` is enabled at compile time (i.e., on Windows).

A build option is added (`capistore`) which can be disabled if this functionality is not desired.

This fixes #18020 but also implements my proposal in #18068 and is built on top of that fix. I can split these out into separate PRs if desired, but the former would preferably be merged before the latter.
pr_comments: Manpage.

I'm not convinced that proposed solution should change existing methods.
Implementation of Store2 API must be enough.

About implementation - it is good to see a provider based sample.  I have a number of engine based implementation including own by_store x509 lookup for openssl before 3.
Also I expect not so generic function names, i.e. with store as part of name. Perhaps current names are acceptable as static functions.
I could not see "error", "expect" and "find" methods. May be "expect" is superseded by "set...param...". If think that other two are required.
P.S.I think that store name could be extracted from URI.
Please register any new URI schemes with IANA: https://www.iana.org/assignments/uri-schemes/uri-schemes.xhtml -- provisional registrations are given on a "first come first served" policy.
This PR is in a state where it requires action by @openssl/otc but the last update was 30 days ago
I strongly support this idea. If I remember correctly, windows has more than one storage (at least, system and user's). Will this code work with it?
@beldmit It uses the system root CA store by default. Since this code uses an URI to specify the Windows store there is the possibility we could allow other stores to be specified.
How do we override this default URI in run-time?
The same way the URI is currently specified, e.g. via an environment variable, see this PR. I could add support for specifying different stores.
It looks better to me if it is overrideable via API.
That is also feasible.
As mentioned here, `capi:` isn't a good scheme name: https://github.com/openssl/openssl/issues/18068#issuecomment-1094849701

> As mentioned here, `capi:` isn't a good scheme name: [#18068 (comment)](https://github.com/openssl/openssl/issues/18068#issuecomment-1094849701)

Suggestion regarding the name: `winstore:`...
non-registration alternative: `org.openssl.winstore:` (same as we did with engines, in #13570)

> > As mentioned here, `capi:` isn't a good scheme name: [#18068 (comment)](https://github.com/openssl/openssl/issues/18068#issuecomment-1094849701)
> 
> Suggestion regarding the name: `winstore:`... non-registration alternative: `org.openssl.winstore:` (same as we did with engines, in #13570)

Fair warning: I'm going to be quite insistent on this
Rebased. Updated to implement option C. URI scheme renamed to `winstore://`.
(it took me a moment to grasp the fact that this is loading certificates only...  :wink:)
Updated. @t8m
@levitte still OK?
Sorry, didn't see this before now.  Yes, still ok
Rebase needed
Given the conflict is just in CHANGES.md which is trivial to resolve, I do not think a rebase is needed, the conflict can be fixed when merging.
Has a request been made to register the URI scheme as per the [comment](https://github.com/openssl/openssl/pull/18070#issuecomment-1095709036) above?

> Has a request been made to register the URI scheme as per the [comment](https://github.com/openssl/openssl/pull/18070#issuecomment-1095709036) above?

The combination of https://www.iana.org/assignments/uri-schemes/uri-schemes.xhtml and https://mailarchive.ietf.org/arch/browse/uri-review/ indicate "no"...

24 hours has passed since 'approval: done' was set, but as this PR has been updated in that time the label 'approval: ready to merge' is not being automatically set.  Please review the updates and set the label manually.

> Rebased.
> 
> @mattcaswell It hasn't. It feels overkill, at least at this stage. What do we want to do? URI registration is specification required. If we want to register it, I'll need to write a spec and push it through the process.
> 
> Wondering what other OpenSSL store providers do.

I'm only aware of PKCS#11, for which there already is a well defined URI scheme: https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc7512

The question to ask is, what if someone else comes up with a `winstore://` URI scheme, independent of this one?  Will their scheme work the same as ours, or will people have to know which library it's sent through for proper use?  After all, "winstore" is a fairly obvious name that anyone could come up with...

It can be argued, though, that we don't have to have that registration in place (even provisional) before the master branch becomes a next release.  That gives us a time frame for doing this.

Also, I might point out that it doesn't necessarily fall on *you* to write the URI spec.  Someone else can do that just as well.

Of course, nothing even comes after `winstore://`. In future we could maybe support named stores since the wincrypt API does have such a feature. `winstore://specific-root-store-name`. But this might be so rarely used so as to not be worth it.

Writing a spec wouldn't take too long, though I wonder how useful this URI scheme is going to be to anyone else. I guess it's conceivably possible other parties using URIs to represent certificate stores might find it useful. So maybe it is worth doing. Or we could go with a scheme name like `vnd-openssl-winstore`. There was an abortive effort to standardise such a scheme: https://lists.w3.org/Archives/Public/uri/2002Dec/0006.html https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/draft-king-vnd-urlscheme-03

> There was an abortive effort to standardise such a scheme: https://lists.w3.org/Archives/Public/uri/2002Dec/0006.html https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/draft-king-vnd-urlscheme-03

There is, of course, that possibility too.

Too bad, BTW, that no one pointed at (or knew about) that draft when we made this:

https://github.com/openssl/openssl/blob/a6843e6ae8ae0551aae8555783f06dab7951f112/apps/include/engine_loader.h#L15-L16

Yeah, if we decide to get it registered, I will just make a PR with a design document for the URI scheme, which should be enough.

@levitte I actually was about to suggest `org.openssl.winstore://` before I found that `vnd-` proposal. Since that proposal was never finalised, and we apparently have a past history of using `org.openssl.engine://`, I suggest we go with `org.openssl.winstore://` for consistency with ourselves.

> @levitte I actually was about to suggest `org.openssl.winstore://` before I found that `vnd-` proposal. Since that proposal was never finalised, and we apparently have a past history of using `org.openssl.engine://`, I suggest we go with `org.openssl.winstore://` for consistency with ourselves.

To be noted: I pushed for `org.openssl.engine://` mainly because engines are on a death path, so that URI scheme would be foreseeably temporary.  Not sure if that impacts how we think about winstore, though, but I thought it was worth mentioning...

issue_context.title: Windows-ROOT as truststore
issue_context.body:
Is there a way to set Windows-ROOT (or any Windows Certificate Store in general) as truststore in openssl?
I think java has some similar feature.

Thanks in advance.
comments:
You could argue that *nix systems use OpenSSL store mechanisme, not the
other way around.

@hlandau 

Thanks for the info and code Hugo.
I did try a similar implementation to what you provided, but was not able to get my connection to work (could be some other issue, checking on it).
As you mentioned, OpenSSL does not have direct code to load from Windows Certificate Store.
Do you know why this is not implemented? Is it because of some known issue or use case limitation?
Just wanted to know from an academic perspective.

> Do you know why this is not implemented? Is it because of some known issue or use case limitation?

In general OpenSSL is an open source software which means a feature gets implemented when someone who needs it submits a code that implements the feature. So the answer is that nobody submitted the code that implements Windows cert store support.

Why nobody did that that's another question which we probably cannot answer.
@t8m Would we be interested in this functionality? I have code to do it lying around and it seems like basically anyone using libssl on Windows will need it. I could make a PR.

I do not see why we would not want it. The difficult question would be how that windows cert store will be enabled. I.E. making it enabled by default on Windows might be considered a too big change for 3.1 by some.
The question for me is would this impact the 3.1 development times?
It's not much code. About 35 lines. I already have it from my own projects. Biggest timesink would just be agreeing the API/how it interacts with existing functions.
Ideally it would be done in terms of OSSL_STORE provider instead of adding certs to X509_STORE which complicates that 35 line code quite some.

A minimum provider that does this only needs an OSSL_STORE loader with export capabilities.  That's enough to handle any key where the key data is programmatically accessible (i.e. exportable) and shouldn't be too hard to do.  The main thing will probably be to design the URI scheme and implement its parser.

... when we do design such a URI scheme, we probably should register it properly too.  I know that I've mentioned the sneaky way of avoiding that, but I frankly think making it official is the better move in the long run.
@levitte See #18070? Currently the issue is that `SSL_CERT_DIR` is interpreted both as a colon-separated list of paths and as a store URI.
